title: The Real Reason SpaceX is Buying Cursor
summary: ByteMonk explains why SpaceX offered $60B for Cursor — and uses the deal as a frame to walk through how Cursor actually works under the hood. The bulk of the video is an architectural breakdown: local indexing, Tree-sitter chunking, a Merkle tree for incremental updates, vector embeddings stored in Turbopuffer, nearest-neighbor retrieval with import-graph expansion, and an execution loop that applies diffs and reads errors. The strategic argument is that the 'interface layer' (Cursor) is becoming more defensible than the model layer, which gives xAI/SpaceX instant entry into agentic coding and a better story for its IPO. No code is written; this is a conceptual walkthrough.
